title: How Inclusively do LMs Perceive Social and Moral Norms?

prompt.location: Appendix C (three prompt variants: zero-shot, zero-shot with option descriptions, zero-shot with a markdown table)
prompt.note: Task: given a Rule-of-Thumb (RoT) from Social Chemistry 101, predict the ordinal social-agreement level (<1%, 5-25%, 50%, 75-90%, >90%).

claim.metric: ADA-Met (Absolute-Distance Alignment, lower=better), zero-shot, r/confessions (CONF) subset
claim.location: Table 1, row "GPT-4 Turbo", Zero-Shot/CONF column (AITA 0.79, ROC 0.79, DEAR 1.02 also given; 100 RoTs per data source, 400 total across CONF/AITA/ROC/DEAR)

data.source: Social Chemistry 101 dataset (400 RoTs with 50 human annotators each; demographics obtained from the dataset creators, Appendix A.2)

notes: gpt-4o-2024-08-06 is also tested in this paper but is not on the live list (only gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 and gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 among the OpenAI models are dated; gpt-4o-2024-08-06 is off-list). Metric compares the LM's ordinal answer to the mode of pre-existing published human annotations (not new human outcomes), computed via ADA-Met (Eq. 1-2). est_calls assumes the headline zero-shot condition only (400 items) at 3 seeds; all three prompt variants together would be ~3x that.
